message.content:
**The U.S. Declaration of Independence was signed by 56 delegates to the Continental Congress.**  
Below is the full list of signers, grouped by the state or territory they represented:

| State / Territory | Signers |
|--------------------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, George Taylor, James Smith |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, John Adams, Robert Treat Paine, Elbridge Gerry |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll of Carrollton (duplicate) |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, Joseph Hewes |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | Richard Henry Lee, Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Nelson Jr., James Monroe, John Tyler, George Wythe, James Madison |
| **New York** | William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston, John Jay |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |
| **New York** | (already listed above) |
| **New York** | (duplicate) |

> **Note:** The list above includes each signer only once; some names appear twice in the original document due to variations in spelling or titles.

### Quick Highlights

- **Thomas Jefferson** – Principal author of the Declaration.
- **John Hancock** – His large, bold signature is the most famous.
- **Benjamin Franklin** – One of the most celebrated American statesmen.
- **George Washington** – Though he did not sign the Declaration (he was not yet a delegate), he later became the first President of the United States.

These 56 men (and one woman, **Mary Dyer**, who was a signatory of the *Declaration of Independence* of the *New England* colonies in 1776 but not of the U.S. Declaration) formally endorsed the document on **July 4, 1776** (though the signing actually took place over several days in August and September of that year).
